chunks: And Pharaoh said: 'O Haman, build for me a tower, that I may reach the reasons (or paths to heaven/God).'
ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh command Haman to build and why?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Ghafir, Pharaoh’s command to Haman to build a 'sarh' (a lofty tower or palace) symbolizes his hubristic attempt to bridge the gap between earth and heaven, asserting his own divinity. Shia exegetes often highlight this as a manifestation of *al-jah* (arrogance) and the human tendency to seek self-sufficiency apart from God, contrasting Pharaoh’s constructed height with the spiritual elevation of the Prophets.
